reason: The Jul 6 - Oct 5 census (log/2026-10-06/init7-sec/census-2026-07-06-to-10-05.json) found a usable 8-K within 20KB in 48 of 2,772 issuer-observation slots (1.7%). A1 keeps N1 only with a usable allowed source, so it would be cash in about 98% of observations and the paired A1-N1 comparison would measure N1 against cash. A2 lets Jev act only where it has a usable source and otherwise follows N1.

arm.input: Identical to A1: the N1 candidate and the archiver's immutable observation for that ticker at the common decision cutoff.
arm.shared_call: A1 and A2 consume the same single Jev call per observation; its usage and cost are charged once to the observation and reported for both arms.
arm.selection: If N1 is cash, A2 is cash. If the archiver status is eligible and the Jev call succeeds, A2 is cash when (catalyst choice is in veto_labels and its confidence >= minimum_veto_confidence) or the dilutive_financing true probability >= 0.5; otherwise A2 holds N1's ticker. In every other case A2 holds N1's ticker.
arm.recording: Persist the A2 decision with its reason before outcomes: n1_cash, no_source, no_causal_source, veto_unavailable, jev_retain or jev_veto. A failed call is never retried and still charges known usage.

evaluation_additions.primary_metric: paired A2 minus N1 USD per initial $100, reported beside paired A1 minus N1
evaluation_additions.coverage: Report per arm the count of observations where N1 selected a ticker, where the veto could act (eligible source and successful call), and where it vetoed.
evaluation_additions.power: At the census rate, a 20-session pilot (120 observations) has about two observations where the veto can act, so A2 minus N1 will usually be exactly zero. The pilot mainly measures N1 against cash and QQQ; Jev's value in this basket needs a broader source or many more sessions. No extension of the window to obtain a favorable result.
